disease_label_per_paper: Alcoholic hepatitis associated with portal venous thrombosis
presentation_summary: 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history presented with three days of generalized sharp abdominal pain, poor appetite, nausea, vomiting, constipation, and new yellow discoloration of the eyes.
He had been drinking half a liter of liquor daily for two years and had gradually stopped drinking over the preceding 10 days.
Exam showed scleral icterus, afebrile state, heart rate 123/min, respiratory rate 18/min, BP 145/65 mmHg, RUQ tenderness, palpable liver and spleen.

Initial labs included hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, MCV 100 fL, WBC 35.5 K/L with neutrophils 83.3%, platelets 198 K/L, sodium 122 mEq/L, total bilirubin 10.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 9.2 mg/dL, AST 306 U/L, ALT 215 U/L, ALP 335 U/L, lactate 4.6 mmol/L, ferritin 2081 ng/mL, MDF 38, and MELD 22.

Hepatitis/EBV/CMV/HIV/hemochromatosis and hypercoagulable workup, portal vein thrombosis imaging confirmation, anticoagulation response, and final diagnosis are kept as confirmatory/non-ranking except the observed presentation ultrasound/abdominal imaging thrombus activity is retained as rankable complication evidence.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Acute viral hepatitis panel did not support hepatitis A/B/C
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Hepatitis B surface antigen negative, hepatitis B core IgM negative, hepatitis A IgM negative, hepatitis C antigen index negative

confirmatory_findings.finding: Additional EBV/CMV/HIV and hemochromatosis workup did not change final alcoholic hepatitis diagnosis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Additional testing for Still's disease, EBV, CMV, and HIV; genetic testing for hemochromatosis was negative

confirmatory_findings.finding: Hypercoagulable workup was pursued before heparin
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: anticardiolipin IgM slightly elevated, antithrombin III and protein C mildly low, Factor V Leiden not detected

confirmatory_findings.finding: Portal vein thrombus resolved after anticoagulation
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: follow-up abdominal duplex ultrasound revealed resolution of the extrahepatic PVT

actual_treatment.name: supportive_alcohol_withdrawal_and_vitamin_care
actual_treatment.source_text_value: IV fluid, pantoprazole, multivitamin, thiamine, folic acid, and lorazepam per alcohol withdrawal protocol

actual_treatment.name: prednisone_40mg_daily
actual_treatment.source_text_value: started on prednisone 40 mg once a day

actual_treatment.name: heparin_then_apixaban_for_portal_vein_thrombosis
actual_treatment.source_text_value: heparin drip and discharged on apixaban 5 mg twice a day for 3 months

outcome.source_text_value: symptoms improved significantly; at 3-month follow-up he was doing well and PVT resolved

quality_warnings: Portal vein thrombosis is retained as a real rankable observed complication axis, not written into the disease name.
Alternative hepatitis and hypercoagulable workup, anticoagulation response, and final diagnosis are confirmatory/non-ranking.
The case has elevated ferritin, lactate, leukocytosis, and abdominal pain that overlap mimics; these are preserved rather than deleted.
